entry: American businessman and founder of [[Amazon (company)|Amazon]], the world's largest e-commerce and cloud computing company. Bezos was the world's wealthiest person from 2017 to 2021, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index and Forbes. He stepped down as Amazon's chief executive in 2021 to become executive chairman. In 2000 he founded the [[Aerospace manufacturer|aerospace manufacturer]] Blue Origin, and in 2013 he bought *The Washington Post*.

American actor and singer, known for leading roles in film and television. He won the Academy Award for Best Actor for playing an alcoholic singer in *Crazy Heart* (2009). His other Oscar nominations include *The Last Picture Show* (1971), *Starman* (1984) and *True Grit* (2010). He also starred in *Tron* (1982) and *The Big Lebowski* (1998), and he received a Cecil B. DeMille Award in 2019.

American musician whose only studio album, *Grace* (1994), attracted a following. His version of Leonard Cohen's [[Hallelujah (Leonard Cohen song)|"Hallelujah"]] became his best-known recording, and *Rolling Stone* named it one of the 500 greatest songs. In May 1997 he drowned in the Wolf River, a tributary of the Mississippi, in [[Memphis, Tennessee|Memphis]], while working on a second album. In 2014 his "Hallelujah" was added to the National Recording Registry of the Library of Congress.

President of the Confederate States (1861–65), leading the Confederacy during the [[American Civil War]]. A member of the Democratic Party, Davis had served in the [[United States Senate]] and as U.S. secretary of war from 1853 to 1857. When the Confederacy was defeated in 1865, he was captured and imprisoned at Fort Monroe, and he was released without trial after two years. The [[Lost Cause of the Confederacy|Lost Cause]] movement honored him as a hero after his release. In the 21st century he has been criticized as a supporter of slavery and racism, and many memorials to him have been removed.

English novelist and former politician. Archer was Member of Parliament for Louth, Lincolnshire, from a 1969 by-election until 1974, and he was deputy chairman of the [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative Party]] from 1985 to 1986. His novel *Kane and Abel* (1979) revived his career, and his books have sold more than 320 million copies worldwide. In 2001 he was sentenced to four years in prison for perjury and perverting the course of justice. He retired from the [[House of Lords]] in 2024.

American [[Serial killer|serial killer]] and sex offender. Dahmer killed and dismembered 17 men and boys between 1978 and 1991, luring many victims to his apartment in [[Milwaukee]], [[Wisconsin]]. Many of the murders involved [[Necrophilia|necrophilia]], cannibalism and the preservation of body parts. He was arrested in 1991 after an intended victim escaped from his apartment. Diagnosed with [[Borderline personality disorder|borderline personality disorder]] and other conditions, he was declared legally sane. He was convicted of 16 counts of murder and sentenced to 16 terms of life imprisonment without parole in 1992. In 1994 he was beaten to death by a fellow inmate.

American financier and convicted sex offender. Epstein made much of his fortune providing tax and estate services to billionaires. In 2008 he pleaded guilty to state charges of procuring a minor for prostitution, in a plea deal that has been criticized as lenient. He was indicted in 2019 on federal charges of sex trafficking minors. He died in custody in [[New York City]] that August before his trial, and his death was ruled a suicide, a finding that is the subject of conspiracy theories. His long associate [[Ghislaine Maxwell]] was convicted in 2021 of sex trafficking girls to him.

American economist and public policy analyst. Sachs is a professor at [[Columbia University]], where he directs the Center for Sustainable Development. From 2002 to 2018 he was special adviser to the [[United Nations]] Secretary-General, and from 2002 to 2006 he directed the UN Millennium Project's work on the Millennium Development Goals. He is an SDG Advocate for the Secretary-General on the Sustainable Development Goals, a set of 17 global goals adopted in 2015. His views on economics, the origin of COVID-19 and the Russian invasion of Ukraine have drawn both attention and criticism.

Nontrinitarian, millenarian and restorationist [[Christian denomination]] that stems from the Bible Student movement founded by Charles Taze Russell. In 1931 Joseph Franklin Rutherford adopted the name Jehovah's Witnesses. Members refuse military service, refuse to salute state symbols such as flags and national anthems, and refuse [[Blood transfusion|blood transfusions]]. They do not observe [[Christmas]], [[Easter]] or birthdays. They believe the present world system will be destroyed at Armageddon and replaced by God's kingdom. Reported worldwide membership was about 9.2 million in 2025. The group has faced government bans in some countries and formal inquiries into its handling of child sexual abuse.

Volcanic island, the largest in [[Korea|South Korea]] (pop., 2020: 673,000), in the [[Korea Strait]]. It covers 1,833.2 sq km and lies 82.8 km south of the Korean Peninsula. The island was formed by volcanic eruptions about two million years ago, and it is dominated by Hallasan, the highest mountain in South Korea at 1,947 m. Its volcanic landscape includes the Jeju Volcanic Island and Lava Tubes, a [[World Heritage Site|World Heritage]] property. A forest growing on [[Lava|lava]] fields supplies the island's main source of [[Groundwater|groundwater]], and it is considered an important wetland. [[UNESCO]] classifies the Jeju language as critically endangered. Jeju is one of the regions of Korea where shamanism is most intact, and tourism is a major part of its economy.

Gelatinous, soft-bodied marine animal, the medusa stage of certain members of the phylum [[Cnidaria]]. A jellyfish has a bell-shaped body with trailing tentacles armed with stinging cells, which it uses to capture prey. Pulsating contractions of the bell propel it through open water. The medusa is normally the sexual stage of a complex life cycle, which produces planula [[Larva|larvae]] that settle as sedentary polyps. Jellyfish live from surface waters to the deep sea and have existed for at least 500 million years, possibly 700 million, making them the oldest multi-organ animal group. The green fluorescent protein of some species is widely used in [[Molecular biology|molecular biology]] research. Swarms can clog fishing nets and the cooling systems of [[Desalination|desalination]] plants, and thousands of swimmers worldwide are stung every year.

American businesswoman, writer and former pornographic film actress. Jameson began appearing in erotic videos in 1993, and by 1996 she had won the "Top Newcomer" award from each of the three major adult-film organizations. She has won more than 35 adult-video awards. In 2000 she co-founded the adult-entertainment company ClubJenna. Jameson had a minor role in [[Howard Stern]]'s film *Private Parts* (1997), and she announced her retirement from pornography at the 2008 AVN Awards. She began working as a webcam model in 2013. In 2025 she said she had left her former lifestyle for the Christian faith.

American actress, known for playing Rachel Green on the sitcom *Friends*. Aniston won a Primetime Emmy Award for the role. Her comedy films, including *Office Space* (1999), *Bruce Almighty* (2003) and *Marley & Me* (2008), cumulatively grossed over $1.6 billion at the worldwide box office. She co-founded the production company Echo Films, and she starred in and produced the Apple TV+ drama *The Morning Show*. She has a star on the [[Hollywood Walk of Fame]].

American actress who began her career as a child model. She made her acting debut in the 1984 film *Once Upon a Time in America*. She won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress for playing Alicia Nash, opposite [[Russell Crowe]], in *A Beautiful Mind* (2001). Her other films include *Requiem for a Dream* (2000), *Hulk* (2003), *Blood Diamond* (2006) and *Top Gun: Maverick* (2022). Connelly was named Amnesty International Ambassador for Human Rights Education in 2005, and in 2012 she became the first global face of the Shiseido Company.

American singer and actress. Hudson finished seventh on the third season of [[American Idol]] in 2004. She won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress for playing Effie White in *Dreamgirls* (2006). Her self-titled debut album (2008) won a [[Grammy Awards|Grammy]] for Best R&B Album. In 2022 she became the youngest woman and third African-American recipient of the EGOT awards (Emmy, Grammy, Oscar and Tony), after winning a Tony as a producer of *A Strange Loop*. Her talk show, *The Jennifer Hudson Show*, premiered in 2022.

American actress and producer. Lawrence won the Academy Award for Best Actress for *Silver Linings Playbook* (2012), becoming the second-youngest winner in that category. Her first Oscar nomination came for *Winter's Bone* (2010). She played the mutant Mystique in the *X-Men* films and Katniss Everdeen in *The Hunger Games* series. She was the world's highest-paid actress in 2015 and 2016, and her films have grossed over $6 billion worldwide. Raised in [[Louisville, Kentucky|Louisville]], she founded the production company Excellent Cadaver in 2018.

American singer, songwriter and actress. After dancing on the sketch comedy series *In Living Color*, she starred in the biopic *Selena* (1997). Her debut album, *On the 6* (1999), included the number-one single "If You Had My Love". She became one of Hollywood's highest-paid actresses through romantic comedies, and her films have cumulatively grossed over US$1.9 billion. Lopez has sold over 80 million records worldwide. She was a judge on *American Idol* from 2011 to 2016.

American actress, model and anti-vaccine activist. In 1993 she began modeling nude for [[Playboy]], and she was later named its Playmate of the Year. She hosted the MTV dating show *Singled Out* (1995–1997) and starred in the sitcom *Jenny* (1997–1998). From 2013 to 2014 she co-hosted the ABC talk show *The View*. McCarthy has promoted the claim that vaccines cause [[Autism|autism]], and she said chelation therapy helped cure her son's autism. Critics have called her views dangerous, and she has described her position as favoring a "pro-safe-vaccine schedule." Large-scale epidemiological research has found no causal link between vaccines and autism.

Taiwanese-born American businessman and electrical engineer who co-founded [[Nvidia]] in 1993. Huang led the company as president and chief executive until his resignation in November 2026. Under his leadership, Nvidia expanded from [[Graphics processing unit|graphics processing unit]] development into high-performance computing and [[Artificial intelligence|artificial intelligence]]. In October 2025 it became the first company to reach a market capitalization of more than $5 trillion. [[Time (magazine)|Time]] magazine included him in its lists of the most influential people in 2021 and 2024. In November 2026 it was reported that he had had multiple extramarital affairs, and he resigned from the company.

Theorem relating the value of a convex function at a mean to the mean of the function's values. Named after the Danish mathematician Johan Jensen, who proved it in 1906, it states that for a convex function f and non-negative weights λ₁, …, λₙ summing to 1, f(λ₁x₁ + … + λₙxₙ) ≤ λ₁f(x₁) + … + λₙf(xₙ). In [[Probability theory|probability theory]], for a [[Random variable|random variable]] X and convex φ, it is stated as φ(E[X]) ≤ E[φ(X)]. The difference between the two sides is called the Jensen gap.

King of [[Joseon]] (r. 1776–1800) and the 22nd monarch of the dynasty. His personal name was Yi San. He was the second son of Crown Prince Sado and succeeded his grandfather, King Yeongjo. Jeongjo continued his grandfather's Tangpyeong policy but prioritized recruiting the most talented scholars regardless of faction. He encouraged the publication of literary collections and legal codes, established the Kyujanggak Royal Library and the Jangyongyeong Guard, and ordered construction of Hwaseong Fortress. His reign is considered one of the high points of the Joseon period, and after the establishment of the Korean Empire he was honored as Emperor Seon. His reliance on the official Hong Guk-yeong left a legacy of state affairs swayed by close retainers. Shortly before his death he chose a crown princess from the Andong Kim clan, a move that became the backdrop for the era of sedo politics.

American television [[Game show|game show]] in which contestants phrase their responses as questions. Created by Merv Griffin, it premiered on [[NBC]] on March 30, 1964, hosted by Art Fleming. The syndicated version, which began in 1984, was hosted by [[Alex Trebek]] until his death in November 2020. Ken Jennings became the sole syndicated host in December 2023. The show has aired over 9,000 episodes, and its daily syndicated version has won a record 45 Emmy Awards.

Any of the nocturnal, hopping desert [[Rodent|rodents]] of the family Dipodidae. Jerboas live in hot deserts across [[North Africa]] and Asia. When chased, they can run at up to 24 km/h (15 mph). Most species have excellent hearing, which helps them avoid nocturnal predators; some are preyed on by little owls in central Asia. The typical lifespan of a jerboa is around 2–3 years.

English philosopher, jurist and social reformer regarded as the founder of modern [[Utilitarianism|utilitarianism]]. He called "the greatest happiness of the greatest number" the measure of right and wrong, and the fundamental axiom of his philosophy. His *An Introduction to the Principles of Morals and Legislation* (1789) was the first major book on utilitarianism. He opposed natural law and natural rights, calling them "nonsense upon stilts," and he advocated freedom of expression, equal rights for women, the separation of church and state, and the abolition of [[Slavery|slavery]] and [[Capital punishment|capital punishment]]. He is also regarded as an early advocate of [[Animal rights|animal rights]]. His students included [[John Stuart Mill]]. On his death he left instructions for his body to be preserved as an "auto-icon", which is displayed at University College London.

English television presenter, journalist and author. He co-hosted the relaunched [[Top Gear (2002 TV series)|Top Gear]] with Richard Hammond and James May, and later co-hosted *The Grand Tour* on Amazon Prime Video. In 2015 the [[BBC]] did not renew his contract after he assaulted a *Top Gear* producer while filming. He hosts the quiz show *Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?* and stars in the farming documentary *Clarkson's Farm*. He writes weekly columns for *The Sunday Times* and *The Sun*, and his controversial statements have drawn criticism.
